newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Aussie sags as bounce proves all-too-brief.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Aussie sags as bounce proves all-too-brief.

text.p: *AUD testing support below 75 cents again after rally faltered in the face of US bank offers with Europeans both sides
*Sentiment hurt by sharp 3.0 point slide in CRB index
*Stops look safe atop $0.7530 now but market still short which may keep 11-month trendline support around $0.7470 intact
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the dollar had sagged to US$0.7481/86 having been up at US$0.7526 overnight from US$0.7515/20 late here Wednesday.

A break and close under the trendline, which currently sits around US$0.7470, would confirm a new phase of the dollar's three-month-old five-cent-wide downtrend was underway which could see it to last year's trough at 73 cents.

A rally above US$0.7530 was needed to counter the immediate bearish mood and it would take a break of US$0.7630/7680 resistance to actually reverse the trend. Such a recovery looked doubtful given market supicions the RBA was set to ease again.

"The market knows that if it chases the dollar higher it would just be making it easier for the RBA to cut," said one. "The Aussie's never going to turn until the market is absolutely certain the easing cycle has ended."

This was easier said than done since the market had thought the cycle was over back in April and May when the RBA emphasised its concerns over wages growth. Instead the bank surprised with a cut on May 23 and a lot of economic data since then had turned out much weaker than expected. So completely had the mood changed dealers supected that if the RBA did ease next month, the money market would start to price in a sixth cut.
A run of strong domestic data might change this view but the next important release is not due until July 2 when retail sales and building approvals for May are out.

And the last rate cut promised to depress consumer price inflation further from the 1.5 percent rate seen in Q1 and some even saw a chance it would turn negative. Such a prospect was bound to fuel pressure for further rate cuts, in a sort of virtuous -- or vicious if you are a dollar bull -- cycle.
Commodities were not offering much support with the CRB index off a hefty 3.04 points to a three month low overnight.
